lines.trans: Opportunities like this do not come every day—he got his MBA in America and leads a team at a foreign investment firm, so go on this blind date, Ye-jin!
When my friend described his ideal type, he said he does not care about age!
And he says he likes fierce, strong women.
How am I fierce at all? Seung-chan, do I seem fierce?
You are not fierce at all—quite the opposite, in fact!
He also likes stylish women like you—you dress great!
Well that part is true, I do dress great! Still, I am just not feeling up for dating right now.
Nobody waits until sparks fly first—feelings grow once you meet! I am giving him your number, so pick up when he calls!
Auntie, could I get one more half boiled egg? I cannot handle spicy food very well.
I am sorry—I already ate mine first earlier…

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Did you hear about this egg?
I was busy today because of egg.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.
I bought bread. And I bought milk too.
Let's eat and then depart.

meanings.note: Used as causal -어서 (까먹어서…).

examples.text: 죄송합니다, 요거는 제가 아까 먼저 까먹어서…
examples.trans: I am sorry—I already ate mine first earlier…
Let us do that (already gobbled up, so…) right away.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 이제 준모도 나이를 먹을 만큼 먹었고 스스로 결정하게 해주시는 게 어떨까요.
examples.trans: Joon-mo is old enough now, so maybe it would be best to let him decide for himself.
Here the word for 'age' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 술 많이 마신 날엔 밀가루 안 먹는다고 했는데 삼선짜장을 시키셔서, 어제 생각보다 많이 마신 건 아니지 않을까요?
examples.trans: He once said he avoids flour after heavy drinking yet ordered black-bean noodles—might he have drunk less than we thought?
Here the word for 'on days when' is key.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: Test
Test2

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 그냥 집으로 가자고 했어야 했는데 나도 술이 땡겼다.
examples.trans: I should have told everyone to go straight home, except I was craving a drink too.
This expression comes from 'was craving'.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used as adnominal (매운).

examples.text: 저 원래 이런 짜고 매운 거 먹으면 안 돼요. 이거 누가 끓인 거예요?
examples.trans: Normally I am not allowed to eat salty, spicy food like this—who made this stew?
It is really spicy compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.en: first, before others, ahead of time
meanings.note: Indicates priority in order or time.

examples.trans: It's late, so I'll head in first.
Who arrived first?

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

examples.text: 난 원래 미소천사인데 반대로 가야지. 천년보살 신디 어때?
examples.trans: I am already a smiling angel, so we should go the opposite way. How about Saintly Cindy?
The topic of in the opposite way came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + -만 (반쪽만).

examples.text: 이모, 계란 반쪽만 더 줘요! 내가 매운 걸 잘 못 먹어서 그래.
examples.trans: Auntie, could I get one more half boiled egg? I cannot handle spicy food very well.
This point about just half is really important.

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.
What is your phone number?
Yes, that's right.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
It really is strongly, boldly compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is strongly, boldly and nice.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 가만히 있는 사람 아주 심란하게 흔들어 놓고, 연애하고 선 보고 소개팅하고!
examples.trans: You shook up someone who was minding her own business, and now you date, do matchmaking meetings, and go on blind dates!
This expression comes from 'going on blind dates!'.

meanings.note: Used as loanword adnominal (스타일리시한).

examples.text: 너처럼 스타일리시한 여자가 좋대, 너 옷 잘 입잖아!
examples.trans: He also likes stylish women like you—you dress great!

examples.text: 그리고 스타일리시한 여자를 좋아한다고 했는데 외모 위주로 판단하는 분은 별로라고 생각합니다.
examples.trans: Plus he said he likes stylish women, and I dislike men who judge women mainly on appearances.

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

Test2

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Contracted form of 이야기하다

examples.trans: Let's talk again later.
Please tell me honestly.

meanings.note: Used as acronym noun (MBA).

examples.text: 이런 자리가 날이면 날마다 오는 게 아니에요! 미국에서 MBA 하고 외국계 투자회사 팀장급이야, 예진이 소개팅하라고!
examples.trans: Opportunities like this do not come every day—he got his MBA in America and leads a team at a foreign investment firm, so go on this blind date, Ye-jin!

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

Today is a (on the contrary) busy day.
The outfit you're wearing today is really pretty.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun (외국계).

examples.text: 이런 자리가 날이면 날마다 오는 게 아니에요! 미국에서 MBA 하고 외국계 투자회사 팀장급이야, 예진이 소개팅하라고!

meanings.note: Used as diminutive pronoun + topic (요거는).

examples.text: 죄송합니다, 요거는 제가 아까 먼저 까먹어서…

examples.text: 이모, 계란 반쪽만 더 줘요! 내가 매운 걸 잘 못 먹어서 그래.
examples.trans: Auntie, could I get one more half boiled egg? I cannot handle spicy food very well.

meanings.note: Used as noun (이상형).

examples.text: 내 친구가 이상형 얘기하는데 걔는 나이를 안 본대!
examples.trans: When my friend described his ideal type, he said he does not care about age!
This point about ideal type is really important.

meanings.note: Used for clothing worn on the body (shirts, pants, dresses, outfits).

examples.trans: I wore a black coat today.
It's cold, so please dress warmly.
There are no seats.
It's my seat.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

전혀.gloss: (not) at all, not in the least

meanings.note: Negative polarity adverb; almost always pairs with a negative verb or adjective (모르다, 없다, 안 ~).

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.
It's not cold at all today.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word for telephone.

examples.trans: A phone call came.
I will hang up the phone.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: Respectful, polite adjective used to apologize in workplaces and to strangers. Formal 죄송합니다 is the standard workplace apology. RR: joesonghada.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for being late.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.

examples.trans: I watched a movie with a friend today.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
